{{short description|Romanian-American mathematician}}
[[File:Mihnea Popa Oberwolfach 2017.jpg|thumb|Popa at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2017]]
'''Mihnea Popa''' (born 11 August 1973) is a [[Romanian Americans|Romanian-American]] mathematician at [[Harvard University]], specializing in algebraic geometry.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=Mihnea Popa, C.V.|website=Department of Mathematics, Harvard University|url=https://www.math.harvard.edu/~mpopa/mini_CV.pdf}}</ref>  He is known for his work on complex [[birational geometry]], [[Hodge theory]], [[Abelian variety|abelian varieties]], and vector bundles.

== Academic career ==
Popa received his bachelor's degree in 1996 from the [[University of Bucharest]]. He studied mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] from 1996 to 1997, and then in 2001 he received his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Michigan]] under the supervision of [[Robert Lazarsfeld]]. His thesis was titled ''Linear Series on Moduli Spaces of Vector Bundles on Curves''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=59931}}</ref> From 2001 to 2005, Popa was a Benjamin Peirce Assistant Professor at [[Harvard University]] and from 2005 to 2007 an assistant professor at the [[University of Chicago]]. He joined the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] as an associate professor in 2007 and became a full professor in 2011. In 2014 he moved to [[Northwestern University]], and in 2020 he became a professor at [[Harvard University]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-23|title=Math Department announces three new faculty members|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2020/06/math-department-announces-three-new-faculty-members/|access-date=2020-08-29|website=Harvard Gazette|language=en-US}}</ref> 

== Awards and honors ==
Popa is an honorary member of the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]].<ref>{{cite web|title=IMAR Honorary Members|website=[[Institute of Mathematics of the Romanian Academy]]| url=http://www.imar.ro/organization/people/honoraryMembers.php}}</ref> He was an [[AMS Centennial Fellowship|AMS Centennial Fellow]] in 2005–2007, a [[Sloan Research Fellowship|Sloan Research Fellow]] in 2007–2009, and a [[Simons Foundation|Simons Fellow]] in 2015–2016.<ref name=CV/> In 2015 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]</ref> In 2018 he was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians ]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref>''D-modules in birational geometry'', ICM 2018, [https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.02375 Arxiv]</ref>
